subsystems.name: Pulsed power supply
subsystems.role: delivers enormous bursts of current in milliseconds, then recharges between shots.

subsystems.name: Accelerator track
subsystems.role: converts that current into a travelling force on the sled.
parts: superconducting coils if cryogenic cooling is used

subsystems.name: Armature and payload bucket
subsystems.role: the moving part that carries the payload and releases it cleanly at the muzzle.

subsystems.name: Guideway
subsystems.role: keeps the sled on a straight, precisely aimed path.
parts: bare track on an airless body

subsystems.name: Payload vehicle
subsystems.role: the cargo itself, which must circularise its orbit after release.
parts: thermal protection if released in atmosphere

subsystems.name: Control and timing
subsystems.role: synchronises switching with sled position to keep acceleration smooth.

buildSteps.title: Pick the site
buildSteps.detail: An airless, low-gravity body such as the Moon allows a bare track aimed near the equator; on Earth the track must sit in an evacuated tube, ideally on high ground, because air drag and heating grow with the square of speed.

buildSteps.title: Build the guideway
buildSteps.detail: Pylons or a tunnel carry a straight track aligned to millimetre tolerances over kilometres, with joints that absorb day–night thermal movement.

buildSteps.title: Lay the accelerator
buildSteps.detail: Coil segments or rails are installed along the whole length in modules, so a failed section can be replaced without rebuilding the line.

buildSteps.title: Build the power plant
buildSteps.detail: Capacitor banks, switches and generators sized to the shot energy are installed at the breech end, with enough generation or storage to recharge between launches.

buildSteps.title: Make the sled
buildSteps.detail: A light armature is bonded to a bucket that holds the payload rigidly under high acceleration.

buildSteps.title: Test sub-scale
buildSteps.detail: Short prototype tracks fire instrumented slugs to measure force, alignment and wear without risking a payload.

buildSteps.title: Creep up in speed
buildSteps.detail: Successive shots raise muzzle velocity, revealing heating, arcing and rail erosion before they become failures.

buildSteps.title: Release and circularise
buildSteps.detail: At the muzzle the payload separates and fires a small stage to raise its perigee, so the ballistic arc becomes a stable orbit.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Launches are spaced to allow cooling, track servicing and recharging, which sets the practical launch cadence.

prerequisites.why: capacitor banks and switches exist, but the combination of energy density, repetition rate and lifetime needed for routine launches does not.
naval electromagnetic catapults and laboratory railguns demonstrate the principle, but nothing has reached orbital velocity outside a vacuum chamber experiment.
they make coilgun tracks more efficient, though they add cooling mass to the system.
vacuum systems exist at kilometre scale in particle accelerators, but not as cheap, reusable launch infrastructure.
the launcher suits bulk cargo, propellant and raw materials far more than people or delicate instruments.
something must add the few hundred metres per second needed to turn the launch arc into an orbit.

pathway.milestone: electromagnetic catapults and laboratory launchers prove force and control
pathway.unlocks: confidence that a long track can accelerate a heavy sled.

pathway.milestone: small-scale demonstrators — a short lunar prototype or an Earth-based suborbital shot
pathway.unlocks: real data on wear, switching and vacuum operation.

pathway.milestone: a lunar launcher delivering cargo to low lunar orbit
pathway.unlocks: routine delivery of water, propellant and structural material off the Moon, where orbital speed is about 1.7 km/s and escape about 2.4 km/s.

pathway.milestone: an Earth launch-assist system, or a full lunar export facility feeding orbital industry
pathway.unlocks: very cheap bulk freight, at the cost of a track hundreds of kilometres long and enormous pulsed power.
